scientific: Meleagris gallopavo (intermedia x merriami, the Sierra foothill birds)

size.note: Tom 1.0-1.25 m bill to tail, 7-11 kg, wingspan 1.25-1.45 m, about 0.9-1.0 m to the top of the head in the alert walk; hen about 0.75-0.95 m, 3.5-5 kg. The build scales the tom to 1.10 m bill tip to tail tip measured along the spine (bill, head, neck base, the back's vertebral line, tail root, tail tip) and stands it 0.95 m to the top of the head (standing_height_m). Straight-line bill to tail in the walking pose 0.76 m; back 0.71 m; belly 0.35 m; tail 0.31 m behind its root; wing cards span 1.27 m. The hen is drawn from the same mesh at about 0.8 scale with _COLORB.

source.prompt: Field-guide side view of a wild turkey tom (Meleagris gallopavo) walking calmly while foraging, the ordinary resting posture, NOT strutting, NOT displaying. Tail feathers closed together into one narrow bundle that points backward and slightly down, not fanned, not spread, not raised. Wings folded neatly up on the back, the wing tips resting on the rump above the tail, not drooping. Body feathers smooth and flat, slim oval body held level, long neck upright, head up. 1.1 m from bill to tail tip, 0.95 m tall. Small bare blue-grey head, red wattles, short snood, short pale bill, black beard on the breast, bronze body, black and white barred flight feathers, long pinkish-grey legs, three forward toes and a hind toe, both feet on the ground. One bird, no base. Clean closed mesh.
source.texture_prompt: Wild turkey tom plumage, natural matte colours with no lighting or shadows baked in: dark bronze body feathers with a coppery green sheen and black feather tips that give a scaled look; folded wings with black primary feathers crossed by narrow white bars, white-barred secondaries and bronze wing coverts; tail feathers dark brown finely barred black with buff-tan tips; rump feathers dark brown with buff tips; bare blue-grey head, red wattles and snood, black hair-like beard, pinkish-grey legs and toes, pale horn-coloured bill, dark eye.
source.head_prompt: A wild turkey (Meleagris gallopavo) of California, one adult male walking on the ground in a relaxed neutral pose, NOT strutting, NOT displaying: body sleek and level with feathers flat, tail folded shut and held level behind as a long narrow wedge, long neck upright, head up. Realistic proportions: 1.1 m from bill to tail tip, 0.95 m tall to the top of the head, long legs. Small bare blue-grey head with red wattles at the throat and a short snood over the bill, short pale bill, a black hair-like beard hanging from the breast, dark bronze body feathers, wings folded tight against the flanks with black and white barred flight feathers, long pinkish-grey legs with spurs, three long forward toes and a hind toe. One bird, no base, no ground. Clean closed mesh.

accuracy_notes: Adopted 2026-10-26 from three Meshy jobs. Reads as a wild turkey tom at 5-30 m: deep bronze body, white-barred secondaries as a pale patch on the flank, wedge tail with paler edges, a thin upright neck with red caruncles and wattle, pale blue head with a snood and horn bill, black beard, long pink-grey legs with spurs; hen colour set (grey head, brown neck, lighter duller body). Still open: the generated covert block on the folded wing stays a dark blue-black patch (real coverts are bronze); the neck is the grafted one stretched 2.7x, so it is thin and its caruncles long; the snood and wattle are coarse at lod1 and procedural at lod2; the tail is narrow (folded) and its buff tip band is not drawn; legs and drumsticks are procedural tubes; the hen is the tom's shape (no smaller head, no shorter legs) and needs the client's 0.8 scale; wing cards are flat, barred spanwise, unslotted. The beard sits low on the breast. A local birder should check the neck length in the walk, the leg length and the body colour against foothill birds.
